title: King's Gambit Accepted
line: Black takes the pawn and guards it with more pawns. White breaks them up.

steps.text: The King's Gambit, accepted. Black guards its extra pawn on f4 with the pawn on g5.
Attack the guarding pawn with the pawn on h2. Pushing the black pawns forward makes them loose.

also.d2d4: That is also sound. This lesson breaks up the pawns first.

steps.text: Do not step back. Jump the knight forward to e5.
steps.after: This is the Kieseritzky Gambit. Black's knight attacks your pawn on e4.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It guards the knight and opens a line for your bishop toward f4.

also.f1c4: Bringing the bishop out is also sound and played as often. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.text: The pawn chases your knight. Step back to d3, where it attacks the pawn on f4.
Take back the pawn on f4 with the bishop. Your knight on d3 helped.
steps.after: Material is level. Black's king side pawns are loose and its knight stands far forward. A sharp fight for both sides.

summary: When Black guards the gambit pawn with more pawns, a pawn from the edge breaks them up and the pawn comes back.
